q: 1. The needle point of the compass should be…… the lead point.
explain: The needle point must be slightly longer than the pencil lead so the needle penetrates the paper while the lead still touches the surface to draw the arc.

q: 2. Drawing board is made of
explain: Softwood like white pine or fir is used because it allows drawing pins to be inserted and removed easily, and 'seasoning' prevents warping.

q: 3. Drawing equipment used by draftsmen primarily as a guide for drawing horizontal lines on a drafting table is
explain: The T-square's blade slides along the working edge of the drawing board, providing a reliable guide for drawing horizontal lines.

q: 4. The working edge of T-square is used to
options: as a base of set square
explain: The T-square serves multiple purposes: drawing horizontal lines, ensuring they are parallel, and providing a base for set squares to draw vertical or inclined lines.

q: 5. To prevent warping of the board ........are cleated at its back.
explain: Battens are wooden strips fixed to the back of the board to prevent it from bending or warping due to moisture or temperature changes.

q: 6. The two parts of T-square are........ and .......
explain: A T-square consists of a 'stock' (the head) and a 'blade' (the long straight edge) joined at a $90^{\circ}$ angle.

q: 7. Angles in multiples of 15 degrees are constructed by the combined use of
explain: By combining $45^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}/60^{\circ}$ set squares on a T-square base, one can achieve angles like $15^{\circ}$, $75^{\circ}$, $105^{\circ}$, etc.

q: 8. Which one is not drafting equipment?
explain: All listed items (drafter, scale, and even a dust cloth to keep the sheet clean) are considered part of the drafting environment.

q: 9. Circles of very small radii are drawn by means of a
explain: A drop compass is specifically used for very tiny circles, where the center point remains fixed while the pencil lead 'drops' and rotates around it.

q: 10. For drawing thin lines of uniform thickness the pencil should be sharpened in the form of -
explain: A chisel edge is used for drawing long, thin, uniform lines (like outlines) because the wide edge wears down more slowly than a point.

q: 11. Which of the following is attached to the compass used to draw large size circle
explain: A lengthening bar is fitted to a compass leg to extend its reach for drawing circles of large radius.

q: 12. ......... is used for drawing curves which can't be drawn by a compass
explain: French curves are templates with various irregular radii used to draw smooth, non-circular curves.

q: 13. To remove unnecessary lines ....... is used
explain: The standard tool for correcting errors or removing construction lines is an eraser.

q: 14. Circle and arcs of circles are drawn by means of a .......
explain: A compass is the primary instrument used for drawing circular geometry.

q: 15. Inking pen is used for drawing ----------- in ink
explain: While technical pens can be used for many things, traditional inking pens were primarily used with guides to draw permanent straight lines.

q: 16. The edge of the board on which T-square is made to slide is called .............
explain: The left (or designated) straight edge of the drawing board, along which the T-square's stock slides, is called the working edge.

q: 17. Set squares are used for drawing ......., ......... and .......... lines.
explain: Set squares are versatile tools used to draw vertical lines, standard angles (30, 45, 60), and parallel lines when slid along a reference.

q: 18. A drafter helps in drawing .............
explain: A drafter (drafting machine) is designed mainly to draw parallel and perpendicular lines quickly and accurately using its scale arms set at fixed angles.

q: 19. Set squares are used to draw
explain: Used alone or with a T-square, set squares can draw vertical lines, inclined lines at fixed angles, and sets of parallel lines.

q: 20. For dimensioning and lettering normally following pencils are used
explain: H is used for thin, precise dimension lines, and HB is used for lettering to make it clear and legible.

q: 21. Parallel lines can be drawn with the help of .............
explain: Parallel lines can be drawn using a mini-drafter, a T-square (sliding along the board edge), or a pair of set squares (one sliding against the other), so all listed tools work.

q: 22. To draw very light line which pencil is used
explain: Harder pencils (like 2H) do not deposit much graphite, resulting in very light construction lines.

q: 23. Extension arm used with engineering compass facilitates .............
options: to draw circles of larger diameter
to adjust distance between the legs
explain: An extension (lengthening) bar attached to a compass increases its radius reach, allowing the drafter to draw circles of larger diameter than the compass alone permits.

q: 24. Stock of T-square makes an angle with working edge
explain: The stock is fixed perpendicular (90°) to the blade so it registers squarely against the board's working edge.

q: 25. A letter B in any pencil denotes .............
explain: In the pencil grading system, 'B' stands for blackness/softness of the lead — higher B numbers indicate softer, darker leads, as opposed to 'H' which denotes hardness.

q: 26. The needle point of the compass should be .......than the lead point
explain: The needle point is set slightly longer so it stays anchored in the paper while the lead point traces the circle.

q: 27. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid triangular tools with fixed straight edges, are used for straight and standard-angle lines but cannot be used to draw irregular curves — that requires a French curve.

q: 28. The diameter of semi-circle is called .............
explain: A protractor's semicircular scale has its straight diametrical edge referred to as the base of the protractor.

q: 29. Mechanical lines are types of
options: line of drawn with free hand
explain: Mechanical lines refer to precise lines created using instruments like scales and T-squares rather than free-hand sketching.

q: 30. Drawing pins/cello tapes are used to .............
explain: Drawing pins and cello tape are used to fix (secure) the drawing sheet firmly onto the drawing board so it does not shift while drawing.

q: 31. The artificial light on the drawing board should be diffused light from the .............
explain: For a right-handed drafter, artificial light should come from the left side (diffused) to prevent the drafting hand and instruments from casting shadows over the working area.

q: 32. In Engineering Drawing, French curves mean
options: drafting tools used to draw non-linear drawings
drafting tools used to draw oblong figures
explain: French curves are drafting templates of varying curvature used to draw smooth non-linear (irregular curved) lines.

q: 33. The following instrument is not used for drawing straight line .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'straight edge' is marked as not used for drawing straight lines in this context; set-squares and the board's working edge are the standard tools/guides actually used for ruling straight lines.

q: 34. During drawing stock of T-square is placed .............
options: adjoining the working edge of the board
adjoining the sliding edge of the board
explain: The stock (head) of the T-square is kept pressed against the working edge of the drawing board, allowing the blade to slide up and down accurately.

q: 35. Clinograph is a type of:
explain: A clinograph is an adjustable set square whose angle can be varied for drawing lines at any required inclination.

q: 36. The drawing prepared by a pencil and without use of drawing instrument is called
explain: Freehand sketching relies solely on the artist's eye and hand coordination without tools like rulers or compasses.

q: 37. For drawing mechanical curves other than circles or circular arcs
explain: Non-circular mechanical curves (ellipses, involutes, spirals, etc.) are drawn using French curve templates.

q: 38. Eraser shield is best used in .............
explain: An eraser shield, which protects surrounding lines while erasing a specific area, is especially useful in detailed hand-drawn perspective drawings where selective correction is often needed without disturbing adjacent linework.

q: 39. A letter B in any pencil denotes
explain: In pencil grading, 'B' indicates a softer, darker lead, as opposed to 'H' which indicates hardness.

q: 40. Pencil drawings are generally corrected or revised with the help of :
explain: An eraser shield is a thin metal or plastic template that allows a drafter to erase small areas without disturbing the surrounding lines.

q: 41. The hardness of pencil lead increases as numeral letter H
explain: A higher number preceding 'H' (e.g. 6H vs 2H) indicates progressively harder, lighter-marking lead.

q: 42. To draw or measure angle is used by.....
explain: A protractor is the instrument specifically designed and graduated for drawing and measuring angles.

q: 43. What is used for drawing curves which can not drawn by compass
explain: French curves are used to draw smooth irregular curves that cannot be produced with a compass.

q: 44. Which of the following is not a drawing hand tool?
explain: An alidade is a surveying sighting instrument, not a basic hand tool for drafting like a straight edge, French curve, or set square.

q: 45. Set squares are not used to draw .............
explain: Set squares, being rigid straight-edged triangles, cannot be used to draw irregular curves, which require a flexible tool like a French curve.

q: 46. A machine which is designed to perform the function of T-square, set square, scale and protractor is .............
explain: A drafting machine is precisely the tool that combines and replaces the functions of the T-square, set squares, scale, and protractor in one adjustable device.

q: 47. Chisel pencils are used to draw .............
explain: A pencil sharpened to a chisel edge maintains a consistent line width when guided along a straightedge, making it best suited for drawing straight lines of uniform thickness.

q: 48. Measurements from scale to the drawings are transferred with the aid of .............
explain: A divider is used to accurately transfer measured lengths directly from a scale onto the drawing sheet without marking or damaging the scale.
